name: TEGAIMON CAFE（テガイモン カフェ） (TEGAIMON CAFE)

claims.text: Signature items mix dairy with fruit (fruit punch includes ice cream; shaved ice includes strawberry-milk toppings), so vegan-suitable juices are prepared in a space where dairy is also handled; no separation protocol is documented.
Menu centers on fresh-cut and hand-squeezed fruit juices and roasted sweet potato, which are naturally plant-based and free of wheat.

name: 焼き芋専門店 維新蔵 ならまち店 (Yakiimo Senmonten Ishingura Naramachi-ten)

claims.text: The signature roasted honey sweet potato is described as additive-free, with its sweetness developed naturally by the potato through 100-day aging and a twice-roasting method — a simple, single-ingredient item that is plant-based and naturally gluten-free.
No published allergen or cross-contamination policy; shellfish are grilled on shared charcoal grills and a celiac should ask for items grilled plain without soy sauce or a shared basting brush.
Sazae tsuboyaki (turban shell) and dipping sauces are commonly seasoned with wheat-containing soy sauce; confirm before eating and ask for no-shoyu preparation if you need strict GF.
Entirely a shellfish/seafood operation with seafood-based grills and broths; not suitable for vegans and cross-contact with animal products is unavoidable.
Plainly charcoal-grilled (素焼き) shellfish and sashimi are naturally gluten-free when served without soy sauce, giving a celiac workable options if requested.

name: bread&coffee te-te (ブレッドアンドコーヒー テテ)

claims.text: Shared kitchen bakes wheat sourdough (自家製酵母パン, パン ¥290–650), wheat castella and pasta alongside the vegan GF items — airborne flour and shared surfaces make cross-contact likely. Not dedicated; risky for celiac.
No published allergen-control protocol; GF is a product category, not a certified celiac program. Ask directly how GF items are separated from wheat baking.
Genuine vegan gluten-free bagels, muffins and cakes made with homemade yeast; raw-food and macrobiotic options.

name: Chaya Ukanomitama (茶屋ウカノミタマ)

claims.text: Shared tourist-market café kitchen with no celiac-specific or wheat-free-kitchen claim; GF items are curated menu items (some likely naturally GF). Cross-contact unverified — ask staff per item.
Vegewel lists GF menu available and vegan/vegetarian modification possible, implying staff accommodate dietary requests; no formal allergy protocol published.
Own-farm pesticide-free (無農薬) herbs and fruit; organic focus; registered Mie health-support shop.
Open 9:00–17:00 year-round; easy sightseeing stop by Meoto Iwa, one stop from Toba.

Owner's claim is that the entire single-product line is rice flour (米粉), including custard and chocolate creams, so wheat flour should not be present — but this is a self-declaration, not a certified allergen-controlled facility; confirm by phone for a celiac child.
「小麦粉アレルギーの方にも安心して…お召し上がりいただけます」— shop states wheat-allergy customers can eat safely.
Whole product line converted to all-gluten-free rice flour (batter + creams); anko naturally wheat-free.
2 minutes from Iseshi Station, on the main Ise Jingu approach route.

name: 炙り味噌らーめん 麺匠 真武咲弥 渋谷店 (Aburi Miso Ramen Mensho Shinbu Sakiya (Shibu)

claims.text: No source confirms separate cooking equipment/water for gluten-free noodles versus the shop's standard wheat noodles; the kitchen prepares both on the same menu.

When you buy the genmai-noodle ticket, staff confirm the allergy at the entrance and explain: because the same kitchen handles regular (wheat) ramen and soy sauce, trace contamination is unavoidable — are you OK with that? (同じ厨房で通常のラーメン（小麦麺）や醤油を扱っているので、微量のコンタミネーションは避けられませんが大丈夫ですかという確認があります)

Reviewer: 'not safe for celiac or gluten intolerant... everything is contaminated with the other ingredients if you are following a strict diet.' At least one celiac reported not feeling well after eating; other celiacs report no reaction — experiences are mixed.

FindMeGlutenFree listing summary indicates the kitchen handles wheat products with shared equipment/prep areas so cross-contact may occur, and that the restaurant cannot fully guarantee accommodation for celiac disease / severe wheat allergy.
各席に小麦不使用のしょうゆを置くなどアレルギーに配慮 (Wheat-free soy sauce is placed at every table as an allergy accommodation).

Owner developed the gluten-free noodle, gluten-free karaage, and vegan ramen lines specifically so customers with wheat allergies or dietary restrictions could eat there; some customers have told him it was the first ramen they were ever able to eat.

Dedicated gluten-free brown-rice (genmai) noodle option made from noodles sourced from a pesticide/chemical-fertilizer-free producer in Shimane Prefecture; a blogger specializing in gluten-free living in Japan wrote it up as a standout GF ramen find in Shibuya.
Four flavors of dedicated vegan ramen (miso, spicy miso, shoyu, shio) at a uniform price, documented by a vegan-focused dining blog.

name: アインソフ ジャーニー 新宿店 (AIN SOPH. Journey Shinjuku)

claims.text: AIN SOPH's kitchen is a shared space where wheat and non-wheat items are prepared together; it is not a dedicated allergen-free facility and the restaurant cannot guarantee that cross-contamination will not occur.

Gluten-free and other allergen items are clearly marked in English on the menu, but a diner who asked staff directly learned that some items labeled gluten-free actually shared a fryer with wheat items or used a non-gluten-free miso — confirming each dish individually with staff is recommended.
Diners have praised the Shinjuku location for its convenient location and clearly available gluten-free options on the menu.
